subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a permanent public plugin safety-event capability, and if so must authorization be bound to host-known plugin identity plus parsed manifest permissions rather than caller-supplied trust data?
rationale: This PR creates a new public Plugin SDK and manifest security boundary for operator-facing safety signals; code review can identify defects, but only maintainers can approve the permanent taxonomy, trust model, and compatibility contract.

options.title: Require host-bound capability
options.body: Approve the direction only after the host constructs a plugin-specific emitter from authoritative registry identity, validated manifest permissions, and runtime payload schemas.

options.title: Keep safety emission core-only
options.body: Do not expose plugin safety-event emission yet; retain trusted core emission until a narrower extension contract is designed.

options.title: Accept caller-supplied policy
options.body: Land the current public helper and treat plugin-provided identity, trust, and declaration inputs as sufficient authorization.

recommendation.title: Require host-bound capability
recommendation.body: Approve the direction only after the host constructs a plugin-specific emitter from authoritative registry identity, validated manifest permissions, and runtime payload schemas.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and review context most strongly connect this person to plugin manifest/API direction and security-sensitive contract decisions.
